notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3h-base..HEAD as usual. SEGMENT e3h: the rest of E3-7: sent-back fireballs and skull kills, fireball trails and shoot events, the darkening under a wither's bar, splash potions on the dragon, withers flying around walls and the glowing wither armour. WAITS: wither-armour needs M3's m3a merged (lightning-drawn's additive pass). wither-flight's wait for D0's d0b (flying.rs) is met: d0b is merged (c0366f3a). If m3a has not merged when this segment is due, run it without wither-armour and add that group to e3z.

No new wire data (darken_screen already travels). Anchors are as of 4301058a: re-check them after the e2b merge. No PROTOCOL bump, no comments in Rust or WGSL, the new file passes rustfmt --check.
